newsitem.title: UK: Stability to stay in Latin America - presidents.
newsitem.headline: Stability to stay in Latin America - presidents.

text.p: Latin America has undergone a silent revolution' that has cast aside a volatile past and turned it into one of the most stable and economically viable areas of the world, leaders from the region said on Monday.
But they told a conference the huge gap between rich and poor remained the key issue to be dealt with.

"The image of economic and political instability still persists even though it no longer applies to our region because real changes have taken place...that constitute a veritable revolution in thinking," Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said.
He and other top Latin American officials were speaking at a conference in London to promote links with the region.
Brazilian President Ferando Henrique Cardoso compared Latin America to the reconstruction of Europe earlier this century.
"In Latin America, the overwhelming feeling today is that we are going through a similar experience, a moment of profound transformation, a silent and peaceful revolution," Cardoso said.
"The changes are clear, strong, and I hope, irreversible."
Political and economic reform had taken hold in the region, drawing in increasing amounts of foreign capital and bringing more social stability, he said.
He noted that the region's inflation, at an average 337 percent three years ago, was just 19 percent last year, while foreign capital inflows had doubled in two years.
"Whereas in the eighties, the world thought of Latin America in terms of debt crisis and economic stagnation, it now sees it as a preferential destination for international investors," Cardoso said.
But he and Fujimori said it was vital to narrow the gap dividing the rich and poor.
"The vast majority of Latin Americans are becoming aware as never before of the enormous abyss that separates our poor backward people from the (rich)," Fujimori said.
The problem of poverty and unemployment can be alleviated with the proper social policies, he added.
